Objective:
Form the Bakunawa!
Relics to sequence: 3

children.name: Message
children.text:
Once upon a time, in the ancient Philippines, Bathala, a supreme god, created seven moons that lit up the earth.

They floated across the night sky, turning darkness into beauty and silence into wonder.

But deep beneath the waves was a scary creature. That creature was Bakunawa, a great serpent-dragon of the sea, who ruled over the ocean. His body wrapped around the world, and his home was cold and shadowy.

One night, he rose from the depths and saw the moons for the first time.

He was amazed.

Their soft glow lit the world in ways he had never known. They were so bright... so beautiful...

And he wanted them, all of them.

And so, one night, Bakunawa leapt from the black ocean and flew into the sky.
He opened his massive jaws and swallowed one moon whole.

As the moon disappeared, the Earth trembled. A terrible earthquake shook the night.
Bakunawa returned to the sea, full and satisfied.
But soon, the moon inside him melted away, like wax near fire.

Furious, Bakunawa tried again the next night. He devoured a second moon.
And again... it melted.

"There are so many moons," he hissed. "I will eat them all!"

Night after night, the serpent struck. And night after night, another moon vanished.

Six moons were gone.


Only one remained.

The people of the ancient islands were afraid.

Each time a moon vanished, earthquakes shook their homes, and darkness filled the skies.

They knew Bakunawa would return, and they had to stop him.

So they learned the sea dragon feared loud noises.

So they gathered their pots, pans, gongs, and drums. And they waited.

On a moonless night, Bakunawa rose once more from the sea.

With a thunderous cry, he soared upwards, mouth opened wide, and wrapped his teeth around the seventh and final moon.

The world began to dim. Shadows spread across the land. It was almost gone.

But then, BANG! CLANG! BOOM!

The people ran to the serpent dragon, shouting:

"Return our moon!"

They banged pots and pans, beat gongs,
 and yelled into the sky. The noise thundered across the land and sea.

Startled and afraid, Bakunawa spat out the moon just before
 swallowing it whole. He roared and went back into the deep and dark ocean.

The moon rose again, casting light on the land. The people cheered and danced beneath its glow.

Little did Bakunawa know, Bathala had seen everything.

To guard the moon forever, Bathala planted tall bamboo trees on its surface. From afar,
 they looked like dark spots, shadows that still remain today.

Bakunawa never gave up. Even now, sometimes, he tries to steal the moon again.

And whenever he does, the people make noise, banging drums, lighting fireworks, and shouting to the skies
 until the moon is safe once more.

Because as long as the bamboo trees stand, and the people remember...

Bakunawa will never succeed.
